grid_constraint_note: PJM capacity auctions reached federal price caps as growing demand outpaced new supply.
tariff_protection_note: Dominion's tariff requires large data centers to make long commitments and minimum payments, although questions remain about costs after the contract ends.
buildout_scale_note: Dominion serves about 450 data centers in Virginia, one of the country's largest data-center markets.
rate_case_note: Dominion says the average residential bill will rise by $11.24 in 2026 and another $2.36 in 2027.
rate_trend_note: The planned bill increases arrive alongside higher PJM capacity costs.

by_the_numbers.label: Average bill increase
by_the_numbers.detail: $11.24 in 2026 plus $2.36 in 2027 for the average residential bill.

by_the_numbers.label: PJM capacity price
by_the_numbers.detail: The 2027/2028 PJM RTO-wide auction cleared at the FERC-approved price cap.

by_the_numbers.label: Data centers
by_the_numbers.detail: Public reporting says Dominion currently serves about 450 data centers in Virginia.

rate_trend_comparison.utility_detail: Dominion says the average residential bill rises $11.24 in 2026 and another $2.36 in 2027.
rate_trend_comparison.national_detail: Computed from EIA STEO July 2026 monthly residential prices: 17.33 cents/kWh in 2025 to 18.72 cents/kWh in 2027.

historical_rate_series.title: Residential average price, bundled service
historical_rate_series.source_detail: EIA Form 861 annual residential bundled-service revenue divided by sales; this is an average retail price, not a tariff.

whats_changed.text: Dominion's large-load tariff takes effect January 1, 2027.

grid_constraint_note: PJM's capacity auction cleared at the federal price cap while AEP Ohio paused new data-center development to implement its tariff.
tariff_protection_note: AEP's data-center tariff requires large projects to cover studies, minimum demand, contract terms, and exit fees.
buildout_scale_note: AEP Ohio reported 17,861 MW of signed data-center load, including tariff and pre-tariff contracts.
rate_case_note: AEP said April 2026 transmission charges rose $7.90 for a 1,000 kWh customer, largely offset by other bill changes.
rate_trend_note: April's changes left the standard-service bill nearly flat even as transmission charges increased.

by_the_numbers.label: Contracted load
by_the_numbers.detail: AEP Ohio reported 5,642 MW under the tariff plus 12,219 MW signed before it.

by_the_numbers.label: Tariff threshold
by_the_numbers.detail: Data centers or expansions of 25,000 kW or greater must use the Data Center Tariff process.

by_the_numbers.label: Net bill change
by_the_numbers.detail: For a 1,000 kWh SSO residential customer, AEP Ohio says April changes net to about $0.22/month.

rate_trend_comparison.utility_label: AEP Ohio April 2026 SSO bill change
rate_trend_comparison.utility_detail: AEP Ohio says transmission rose $7.90, generation fell $7.16, and distribution fell $0.52 for a 1,000 kWh SSO customer.
rate_trend_comparison.national_detail: Computed from EIA STEO July 2026 monthly residential prices: 17.33 cents/kWh in 2025 to 18.31 cents/kWh in 2026.

historical_rate_series.title: Residential average price, bundled service
historical_rate_series.source_detail: EIA Form 861 annual residential bundled-service revenue divided by sales; this is an average retail price, not a tariff.

whats_changed.text: AEP Ohio reported 5,642 MW of binding contracts under the Data Center Tariff.

grid_constraint_note: Georgia Power's approved plan anticipates about 8,500 MW of new electric load over six years.
tariff_protection_note: Georgia requires large-load customers to make upfront contributions, long commitments, and financial guarantees.
buildout_scale_note: Georgia Power reported nearly 2 GW of new customer contracts and forecasts 8,448 MW of additional growth.
rate_case_note: Georgia regulators approved a base-rate freeze through at least 2028, separate from storm costs.
rate_trend_note: Georgia Power says large-load revenue could support typical residential savings, while storm costs remain separate.

by_the_numbers.label: New contracts
by_the_numbers.detail: Georgia Power filed nearly 2 gigawatts of new customer contracts with the Georgia PSC.

by_the_numbers.label: Projected growth
by_the_numbers.detail: Georgia Power forecasts 8,448 MW of projected growth between winters 2025/2026 and 2030/2031.

by_the_numbers.label: Customer benefit
by_the_numbers.detail: Georgia Power says large-load revenue should provide benefits equivalent to $8.50/month for a typical 1,000 kWh residential customer.

rate_trend_comparison.utility_detail: Georgia PSC approved freezing Georgia Power base rates through at least 2028, excluding storm costs.
rate_trend_comparison.national_detail: Computed from EIA STEO July 2026 monthly residential prices: 17.33 cents/kWh in 2025 to 18.72 cents/kWh in 2027, the latest full forecast year in the workbook.

historical_rate_series.title: Residential average price, bundled service
historical_rate_series.source_detail: EIA Form 861 annual residential bundled-service revenue divided by sales; this is an average retail price, not a tariff.

whats_changed.text: Georgia Power filed nearly 2 GW of new customer contracts with the Georgia PSC.
